data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word 'meri' meaning 'sea' and 'dith' meaning 'mighty one'. This name has been used in both English and Scottish cultures. The name Meridith carries the meaning “Mighty one of the sea” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Meridith usually hope their child will grow to embody mighty one of the sea and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Meridith total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Meridith may have originally referred to a god or goddess of the sea, or someone perceived to have great power over the sea due to their profession or lineage. This connection to the sea, water, and aquatic life can still be seen in some of the symbolism associated with this name, such as the mermaid. Its use in Scotland may have also brought about associations with the Clan MacDeith, who were described as sea-rovers.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Meridith, with its origins in Old English and potential associations with gods or goddesses of the sea, carries a rich spiritual significance. It can serve as a reminder of God's power over the waters and His provision of sustenance through the sea. The name can also be seen as a call to trust in God's protection, strength, and guidance, much like how a ship in the sea relies on its captain for safe passage. Ultimately, the name Meridith provides a powerful connection to both the natural world and the divine, and can serve as a meaningful reminder of the expansiveness and resilience of faith.
